code.why: The host process around the fetch: the life and the published examples drive the pack's fetch in their own in-memory Worlds, never this standalone listener; conformance's standalone check starts it and reaches the World's boot probe through it (architecture, Coverage and Conformance).

An object is written only after its blob; refresh similarly keeps its requested bytes. No vendor call deletes only its backing blob while retaining a live row. This guards corrupt engine/blob state in reads and copies, not a documented vendor refusal.

The World's GET /twin/board door computes the paths of static HTML assets for its board pages; no customer API or vendor-page request calls this helper. Its parent board declaration uses the same door.

The kernel calls these only from GET /twin/board, the World board door. Vendor API and dashboard requests do not invoke the board projection. Architecture Coverage permits door declarations; servedAt projects the same door’s HTML pages.

The manifest performs hooks invoke these only when deploying an entry against a real root. They reopen a real vendor upload session, send held asset bytes and replace its completion token. The in-memory customer and example fetch walks do not perform entries at a real root. Architecture Coverage excludes the real vendor side from a World fetch walk.
